text:
maria: Quick check — post-launch messaging split looks like this: webinar registrants conversion +15% but inbound route count from GA4 is ~430 vs internal 312. Anyone digging into the router?
ajay: Saw the spike, thanks. GA4 click->session attribution defaults to a 24h window. Internal lead router uses 7d cookie attribution — that could account for differences. :thinking:
kevin: quick query I ran:
```
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM prod.leads
WHERE campaign = 'launch-webinar'
AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-03-15' AND '2026-03-22'
```
Result: 312 (internal DB).
sophia: +1 on attribution window. Also seeing inconsistent UTM casing from partner feeds — ~40 leads with 'Launch-Webinar' or 'launch_webinar' variants, so our parser may drop them.
maria: Good catch. Also note messaging split: 30% of registrants were sent to SDR-B via the new routing rule; SDR-B tags are currently excluded from the marketing dashboard.
ajay: Proposed actions:
1) Normalize UTM parsing and backfill
2) Re-run attribution using session-level join for GA4 vs internal
3) Update dashboard to include SDR-B tag
cc @deckbot please kick a dashboard-refresh job now :eyes:
deckbot: scheduled job 'dashboard-refresh' started, ETA ~90s.
deckbot: job 'dashboard-refresh' completed successfully — figures refreshed.
kevin: After refresh totals now show 421 in marketing dashboard. Narrowed gap to ~11 vs GA4 (430). Might be client-side drop or bot filtering.
sophia: I'll sample 50 raw form POST logs vs created leads to check JS error/drop patterns.
maria: Thanks team. Let's reconvene tomorrow 10:00am PT. Action owners: ajay (attribution re-run), kevin (backfill query + reconciliation), sophia (form audit). :thumbsup:
